title: Global Risks Report 2026
key_claim: 68% of respondents describe the next 10-year political environment as 'multipolar or fragmented order in which middle and great powers contest, set and enforce regional rules and norms'; only 6% expect a return to unipolar rules-based order; geoeconomic confrontation tops the most-likely-trigger list for material global crisis in 2026.
notes: Structural anchor for the consensus framing of the multilateral vacuum. WEF runs annual elite survey across 1,500+ leaders.

publisher: Australian Government — Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet
title: Australia-Japan Joint Statement on Elevated Critical Minerals Cooperation
key_claim: A$1.67bn Australia-Japan critical minerals declaration (4 May 2026) — most substantive bilateral minerals commitment in shared history — explicitly built on prior Australia-US Critical Minerals & Rare Earths Framework, establishing parallel allied diplomatic tracks designed to counter China's dominance.
notes: Tier 1 government primary source — the joint statement itself.

title: From safety to impact: what India's AI summit signals about global governance
key_claim: India AI Impact Summit (16-21 Feb 2026, Bharat Mandapam) marked completion of the Bletchley → Seoul → Paris → Delhi succession; pivot from safety/governance to 'practical impact' anchored in voluntary contributor networks rather than treaty obligations; explicitly positioned as Global South alternative to EU/US/China models.

title: Sovereignty, safety, and scale: Takeaways from the India AI Impact Summit
key_claim: India AI Impact Summit institutionalised a light-touch Secretariat, informal semi-annual Steering Group, and voluntary contributor networks — explicitly designed not to converge on a single regulatory model, allowing countries to access, adapt, and deploy resources within their own governance frameworks.
notes: Tier 2 institutional research; corroborates IISS framing with focus on the Secretariat structure as a model for emerging mini-lateral governance.

title: Safety should be front and center in India's vision for its AI Impact Summit
key_claim: Atlantic Council critique of the AI summit succession argues the 'safety to impact' pivot risks losing the original Bletchley mandate; explicitly frames the summit series as the de facto AI governance forum that has displaced UN-system processes.
notes: Tier 2 institutional research; useful for the counter-argument's policy concerns about mini-lateral fragility.

title: Just what we need: US calls key countries together on critical minerals
key_claim: 2026 Critical Minerals Ministerial in Washington brought together representatives from 54 nations and the EU; smaller coalitions of trusted partners 'can align policy, capital and industry in ways that global frameworks can't', with Australia, Canada, US, Japan, Korea forming nucleus capable of supporting resilient diversified value chains.
notes: Tier 3 quality think-tank journalism (ASPI The Strategist).

title: South Africa Confirms it Won't Attend the G20 in Washington
key_claim: South African Finance Minister Enoch Godongwana and SARB Governor Lesetja Kganyago not accredited by US for 16 April 2026 G20 Finance Ministers meeting in Washington; Godongwana: 'the US has not accredited us, which means South Africa will not be part of the G20 for the whole of this year'.
notes: Tier 3 quality journalism — most decisive recent example of the universal-membership norm being broken.

title: US, Japan lay critical mineral bloc foundation
key_claim: US-Japan Action Plan on Critical Minerals signed 19 March 2026 explicitly designed to move beyond bilateral cooperation toward a coordinated, multinational supply chain strategy aimed at countering China's dominance; explicitly framed as foundation for plurilateral framework.
notes: Tier 3 specialist trade press; corroborates the mini-lateral architecture build-out for critical minerals.
